clue.text: Country stripper finds position next to the West End

parts.note: a locus is a position or place, especially in mathematics

indicators.note: the End of the word West is its final letter, tacked on after the position

explanation.surface: A rural striptease artist lands a spot near London's theatreland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like London's theatre district, but 'End' only picks the final letter of 'West'.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarms of these insects strip the countryside of every crop, hence a stripper of the land.

clue.text: Light cover helps Adam, being awkward

indicators.note: being awkward means the letters of helps Adam are arranged clumsily into a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Adam awkwardly lends a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade fitted over a bulb covers the light.

clue.text: Ace led by North American among players in card game

indicators.note: the ace is led by the rest, coming after it
among puts the North American inside the word for players

parts.note: the cast are the players in a show
A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: An ace is played first by a North American among the players of a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: Ace is the last letter, preceded (led) by the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: This rummy-type game played with two packs is a well-known card game.

clue.text: It starts to make hand jump forward

definitions.text: It starts to make hand jump forward

parts.words: It starts to make hand jump forward
parts.note: describes a season whose beginning sends the hour hand of the clock on by an hour

explanation.surface: Something begins that makes a hand leap ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The hand is a clock's, put forward an hour when British Summer Time begins in spring.
explanation.definitionFit: Daylight-saving time begins with clocks set one hour ahead.

clue.text: Decade proceeded with external restraints

indicators.note: the restraints are said to be external, so they sit around the word for proceeded

parts.note: ties are bonds or restraints
proceeded means went

explanation.surface: Ten years went by with someone kept in bonds.
explanation.definitionFit: The years numbered from 20 to 29 of a century make up one decade, such as the roaring one of the 1920s.

clue.text: Keen fighter takes marines forward into dicey situation

indicators.note: into puts the marines and forward inside the bet

parts.note: a wager is a bet, a situation where one gambles
RM stands for the Royal Marines
on means forward, as in 'go on'

explanation.surface: An eager soldier pushes the marines ahead into a risky spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone keen on war, a fighter by inclination, is an advocate of war.

clue.text: An 'efty chap turns up with a reputation

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a hefty chap is a he-man; drop the h as the apostrophe in 'efty does and he-man becomes 'e-man

explanation.surface: A burly Cockney fellow arrives carrying a reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''efty' tells you to drop the H, so the hefty HE-MAN becomes E-MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: One's good name is one's reputation, as in 'make a name for yourself'.

clue.text: National PM losing his head

indicators.note: the Prime Minister loses his head, the first letter of his name

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a Victorian British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister of the country is beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: A national of Israel is a citizen of that country.

clue.text: Bomb is not half an unpleasant experience

indicators.note: not half of the word is is kept, losing its first letter

parts.note: a hell is a very unpleasant experience

explanation.surface: A bombing isn't half a nasty ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' is British slang for 'very much', but here it halves 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An explosive projectile fired from a gun is a shell, a kind of bomb.

clue.text: Small island bird, not loud

indicators.note: loud is F, forte in music, which is taken out

parts.note: a finch is a small bird

explanation.surface: A tiny island songbird keeps quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland an inch is a small island, as in Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish word, from Gaelic innis, names a small island.

clue.text: One living on island with a calf

definitions.text: One living on island with a calf

parts.words: One living on island with a calf
parts.note: reads like a farmer with a young cow, but the island is the Isle of Man, which has a small islet called the Calf of Man off its southern tip

explanation.surface: An islander keeps a single young cow.
explanation.walkthrough: The Calf of Man is a small island just off the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea; 'calf' wants to be livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Isle of Man takes his title from the island and its Manx adjective.

clue.text: Pity about bit of food not being finished

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the word for the bit of food is left unfinished, losing its final letter

parts.note: a morsel is a small bit of food

explanation.surface: Sorrow over a scrap of food left uneaten.
explanation.definitionFit: In an older sense the word meant pity or compassion, not just regret for one's own wrongs.

clue.text: Nuns resist ill-designed bead-gear

indicators.note: something badly designed is put together wrongly, so the letters of resist are rearranged

parts.note: a hood is a covering worn on the head

explanation.surface: Nuns refuse a badly made piece of headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious community of women, such as an order of nuns, is called a sisterhood.

clue.text: Unpopular doctor came down to earth

definitions.meaning: the doctor of the old rhyme 'I do not like thee, Doctor ...', written about an Oxford dean nobody liked
dropped to the ground, past tense of the verb to fall

explanation.surface: A disliked physician crashed to the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'I do not like thee, Doctor Fell' is a well-known English nursery verse about an unloved dean.
explanation.definitionFit: The disliked Dr of the rhyme shares a name with the past tense of fall, meaning dropped to the ground.

clue.text: Animal may have trouble initially with limb going over one in road

definitions.text: Animal may have trouble initially with limb going over one in road

indicators.note: in a down clue the limb goes over, above, what follows

parts.note: a cat is an animal

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of trouble

parts.note: a leg is a limb

indicators.note: in puts the one inside the road

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A beast struggles to put a leg over something set in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines it: a grid of bars across a road that livestock cannot walk over.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid of spaced bars in a road lets vehicles pass but stops livestock, whose legs slip between them.

clue.text: A father without exercise, 'e should be made fit

indicators.note: here without means outside, so the father goes around the other pieces

parts.note: dad is an everyday word for father
PT is physical training, exercise
'e is he with the h dropped, as in Cockney speech, leaving just E

explanation.surface: A dad who skips exercise should be got into shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense 'outside', not 'lacking'; the dropped-h 'e gives a lone E inside DAD with PT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something altered to suit a purpose has been fitted or modified for it.

clue.text: Avoid fish and poultry when young

parts.note: to duck is to avoid or dodge
lings are fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Steer clear of seafood and young birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Young ducks, farmyard fowl in infancy, are poultry when young.

clue.text: Fag-end sailor put down pavement grille

indicators.note: the sailor is put down after the end letter, following it in the answer
the end of the word fag is its last letter

parts.note: a rating is an ordinary sailor in the navy

explanation.surface: A sailor stubs out a cigarette butt on a drain cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fag' is British slang for a cigarette, so 'Fag-end' is a butt; here it picks the last letter of 'Fag'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid of bars set in a pavement over a drain or cellar is a type of grille.

clue.text: What injured soldier may have received' — fruit and hospital books

definitions.text: What injured soldier may have received

parts.note: grapes are fruit
H is the map abbreviation for hospital
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A wounded soldier gets grapes and books in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: Grapes and books are typical hospital gifts, but the soldier received cannon fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannon shot of small iron balls fired in a cluster is what a wounded soldier may have been hit by.

clue.text: Purgative medicine getting rid of one's disease

indicators.note: a purgative churns the insides, so the letters of medicine are stirred up
the letter for one is removed from the medicine before rearranging

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A laxative cures someone's illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purgative' looks like part of the definition but is the anagram signal: MEDICINE less I rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a noun, the word means a disease constantly present in a particular region or people.

clue.text: Investigate about ship's drift

parts.note: to dig is to investigate
re means about
SS is a steamship

explanation.surface: Look into the course a vessel is drifting on.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander off the point in talk is to drift from the subject.

clue.text: If a sailor returns, then get a liqueur

indicators.note: the words If a sailor go back the other way, read right to left

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: If a sailor comes home, have a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: This almond-flavoured cordial is a sweet liqueur, also the name of a small biscuit.

clue.text: Fluid that comes with a plant

definitions.text: Fluid that comes with a plant

parts.note: fl abbreviates fluid, as in fl oz
a vine is a climbing plant

explanation.surface: A liquid supplied together with a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes a yellow dye and antiseptic once extracted from oak bark.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow dye, used as an antiseptic solution, was first obtained from the bark of a tree.

clue.text: Free sheet with a piece of Indian music

parts.note: a rag is a cheap newspaper, here one given away free

explanation.surface: A giveaway newspaper comes with a sample of Indian music.
explanation.definitionFit: In classical Indian music this is a melodic framework for improvisation, and a piece built on it.

clue.text: Immoderate language restricted by beast? The opposite:

indicators.note: being restricted by words means being held inside them
the opposite way round: the beast is held by the words Immoderate language, not the reverse

explanation.surface: Wild talk is curbed by an animal, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, the language is restricted by the beast; 'The opposite' turns it so the beast sits inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: The honey badger of Africa and Asia is a fierce beast.

clue.text: Not showing any diversity yet

explanation.surface: Lacking any variety even so.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both identical in every case and nevertheless, as in 'thanks all the same'.

clue.text: Carry kid on back of bike

indicators.note: in a down clue the kid sits on, above, the letter that follows

parts.note: a tot is a small child, a kid

indicators.note: the back of the word bike is its last letter

explanation.surface: Give a child a ride on the rear of a bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote something is to carry or lug it.

clue.text: Hypocrite making a pile, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the word is said aloud and sounds like another

parts.note: a heap is a pile

explanation.surface: A two-faced person piles up money, rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: The hypocrite is Uriah, the fawning clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Uriah of David Copperfield, always 'umble', is the classic literary hypocrite.

clue.text: Check on article in that respect.

indicators.note: in an across clue the check goes on, that is after, the article

parts.note: the is the definite article
a rein checks or restrains a horse

explanation.surface: Inspect an item in that regard.
explanation.definitionFit: The formal adverb means in that place or matter, in respect of that.

clue.text: A mountain lake is hard to sully

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
taken as written
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A mountain lake is difficult to pollute.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarnish is to stain, dull or spoil a surface or a reputation, the same as to sully it.

clue.text: Most recent employment suggests retirement is imminent

definitions.meaning: the latest job one has held
the bugle call sounded at night to tell soldiers to retire to quarters, also played at military funerals

explanation.surface: Your latest job hints that you will soon stop working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' looks like leaving work but is soldiers retiring for the night, signalled by the bugle call.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both the latest position held and the military bugle call announcing the end of the day.

clue.text: In our time 'green' is used to attract consumers

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, marks dates in the present era
vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: Nowadays being eco-friendly is a marketing ploy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' wants to mean eco-friendly, but it is the heraldic colour VERT.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial announcement is the thing put out to draw in buyers.
